title: Key figures (calculated on the pack)
body:
- Business: wholesaler of supplies for bakeries and pastry shops, and of BOF products (butter, eggs, cheeses… and dairy) — Toulouse and Haute-Garonne.
- Catalogue: 71 products (67 active today), 10 families: flours and milling, yeasts, sourdoughs and improvers, butters and fats, dairy and egg products, sugars and pastry ingredients, chocolate and cocoa, dried and candied fruit, raw viennoiserie and frozen doughs, fresh fruit for pastry, packaging and shop items.
- Portfolio: 104 customers — 88 active, 9 lost (no orders any more), 3 blocked, 4 prospects.
- Active customers by type: 43 retail shops, 11 restaurants, 9 supermarkets, 8 brasseries, 6 contract catering, 6 caterers, 5 hotels.
- Revenue delivered over 12 months: approximately **€8,983k excl. VAT** (€2,060k over the last 90 days), 8,295 orders delivered, average basket ~€1,083 excl. VAT.
- Order channels (12 months): phone 40%, e-mail 24%, WhatsApp 22%, web portal 15%.
- Top customers by revenue (12 months): Hyper Garonne Fenouillet (cli_0004), Hyper Garonne Ramonville-Saint-Agne (cli_0104), Proxi Fraîcheur Saint-Aubin (cli_0062), Maison Sarrailh (cli_0001), Le Fournil de Labège (cli_0050).
- Star products by revenue (90 days): 82% laminating butter (2 kg sheet), T55 traditional French wheat flour (25 kg bag), Raw frozen all-butter pain au chocolat 75 g (carton of 140), Raw frozen all-butter croissant 70 g (carton of 150), AOP Charentes-Poitou 84% laminating butter (2 kg sheet), UHT liquid cream 35% (1 L carton), Frozen par-baked baguette 280 g (carton of 60), AOP Charentes-Poitou unsalted butter (carton of 10 × 1 kg).
- History: 3 years of data (since 25/11/2023): orders, purchases, batches, invoices, payments, rounds.

title: History
body:
- 1994: Jean Castagné, a former sales representative for a flour mill, opens a depot for flours and yeast in Fondeyre with a single lorry.
- 2001: butter, cream and eggs added: the depot becomes a proper BOF supplier for bakers.
- 2008: first frozen store (-20 °C) for raw viennoiserie and puff pastry.
- 2013: Bernard Castagné, the son, takes over the business; launch of packaging and Epiphany items (crowns, charms).
- 2019: contract with two supermarket chains for their in-store baking terminals.
- 2022: surge in the price of butter and flour: switch to monthly rather than annual pricing.
- 2024: listing of organic flours from the Moulin de l'Arrats (Gers) and launch of a Tarn-Lauragais round.
- 2026: ordering by WhatsApp rolled out across the business, switchboard open from 5:30 a.m.

title: House rules
body:
- Here they say “chocolatine”, never “pain au chocolat”: both words refer to the same SUR-PAC item, and the agent must not correct the customer.
- Flours are sold by the 25 kg bag (except einkorn, in 10 kg bags): “10 de tradi” = 10 bags of T55 traditional flour, not 10 kg.
- Butter and chocolate prices are reviewed on the 1st of each month; flour prices quarterly, depending on the wheat price.
- Galette des rois: pre-orders for ground almonds, puff pastry, crowns and charms must be placed before 15 December, otherwise stock is not guaranteed.
- In Toulouse they also make the couronne des rois (an orange blossom and candied fruit brioche): candied fruit and orange blossom water go as quickly in January as ground almonds.
- Free-delivery threshold €150 excl. VAT; below that, delivery costs €12. Pallets and insulated crates are collected by the driver.
- Bakeries are often closed on Monday or Wednesday: never promise a delivery on a closing day, check the customer record.
- Flour bags are paid for by LCR (bill of exchange) at 30 days end of month for bakers; cash payment for new customers for the first three months.

title: Convention for "now" in the pack
body: The pack is frozen at **Tuesday 24/11/2026 at 06:30** (Paris time). Today's orders are prepared, confirmed or still in draft; the lorries have not left. Tomorrow's orders are still arriving. The history covers three years.

title: The 24-hour cycle
body:
- **05:00** — Rémi opens the loading bay: receiving lorries (flour, butter, frozen goods) and checking temperatures.
- **05:30** — Lucie takes the switchboard: bakers call after the first batch for a yeast or flour top-up.
- **06:00** — End of round preparation; frozen crates are loaded last.
- **06:30** — First rounds leave. **This is the « now » time of the pack.**
- **07:00** — Deliveries to bakeries and pastry shops from 7 a.m. to noon (after the morning rush).
- **09:00** — Sales reps are out visiting customers; Thierry compares butter and flour prices.
- **13:00** — Bakers place their afternoon orders (phone, WhatsApp, portal).
- **15:00** — Thierry places supplier orders for the next day or the day after.
- **17:00** — Order cut-off for tomorrow morning's rounds; night preparation of long rounds.

title: Order cut-off times
body:
- Order before 5 p.m. for next-morning delivery (Toulouse and outskirts rounds).
- Lauragais-Tarn round (Tuesday and Friday): order the day before before noon.
- Same-day yeast and flour top-up: possible until 9 a.m. if the round has not left, otherwise collection at the depot.
- Epiphany: pre-orders of almond powder, puff pastry, crowns and charms before 15 December.
- Community catering: purchase order at D-3 before noon.

title: Who calls when
body:
- Sales reps (Julien, Marion, Karim) take orders from their own portfolio during the day.
- No night switchboard: messages left in the evening are handled when the office opens.
- Orders received by e-mail and WhatsApp arrive as drafts and are confirmed by the sales administration (ADV) or the sales rep.

title: Invoicing
body:
- Invoice on delivery, weekly (on Monday, for the previous week) or monthly (on the 1st) depending on the customer.
- `overdue` is never stored: an invoice issued or partially paid after its due date is overdue.
- Returns and refusals at delivery are deducted from the invoice (prepared line reduced).

title: Ambiguous aliases: always resolve doubt
body:
- “laminating butter”: AOP Charentes-Poitou 84% laminating butter (2 kg sheet) (prd_0025) or 82% laminating butter (2 kg sheet) (prd_0026) or Puff pastry margarine (10 kg carton) (prd_0030). “All-butter” artisans want the AOP laminating butter or the 82%; the margarine only if the customer says “marge”. Ask AOP or standard, as the difference is more than €2 per kilo.
- “milk”: Whole UHT milk (1 L carton) (prd_0033) or Milk couverture chocolate 38% (pistoles, 5 kg bag) (prd_0040). “Some milk” on its own = cartons of whole milk; “38 milk” or “milk couverture” = chocolate. A pastry chef who talks about Easter is talking about chocolate.
- “powder”: Blanched ground almonds (5 kg bag) (prd_0046) or Roasted hazelnut powder (1 kg bag) (prd_0048) or Cocoa powder 22-24% (1 kg bag) (prd_0043) or Cold-set crème pâtissière mix (10 kg bag) (prd_0021). In January, “some powder” is almost always the ground almonds for galettes. Otherwise ask them to specify almond, hazelnut, cocoa or custard powder.
- “flour”: T55 traditional French wheat flour (25 kg bag) (prd_0001) or T55 baker's wheat flour (25 kg bag) (prd_0002) or T45 gruau pastry flour (25 kg bag) (prd_0003) or T65 country wheat flour (25 kg bag) (prd_0004). A baker with no specification = their usual flour (see their history); a pastry chef = T45 gruau. Always confirm the number of 25 kg bags.
- “chocolate”: Dark couverture chocolate 64% (pistoles, 5 kg bag) (prd_0038) or Baker's chocolate sticks 44% (1.6 kg carton, 300 sticks) (prd_0042) or Dark chocolate baking chips (5 kg bag) (prd_0044) or Raw frozen all-butter pain au chocolat 75 g (carton of 140) (prd_0054). “Some pains au chocolat” = frozen viennoiserie SUR-PAC; “some sticks” or “chocolate for the pains au chocolat” = BAT-CHO; “some couverture” = pistoles.
- “cream”: UHT liquid cream 35% (1 L carton) (prd_0031) or Thick crème fraîche 30% (5 L tub) (prd_0032) or Cold-set crème pâtissière mix (10 kg bag) (prd_0021). By default, 35% liquid cream in cartons. “Crème pât” = the crème pâtissière powder, in a 10 kg bag.

title: Our customers
body:
- **Artisan bakeries** (38 customers): Lauragais traditional flour only. AOP laminating butter for viennoiserie, pastry butter for the rest.
- **Pastry shops, chocolatiers and tea rooms** (12 customers): Always the same couverture, same origin. Red berries from Lot-et-Garonne in season.
- **Restaurants and bistros** (15 customers): Cream and eggs twice a week. Raw croissants for the Sunday brunch.
- **Sandwich shops and snacking franchises** (8 customers): Orders through the portal. Wants a fixed price per carton for the year.
- **Supermarket bakery counters and in-store baking units** (10 customers): Orders by e-mail quoting the store's order number. Delivery to the loading bay before 8 a.m.
- **Caterers and event organisers** (8 customers): Large orders at J-2 for events. Mini viennoiseries for seminars.
- **Hotels (breakfast and restaurant)** (7 customers): Mini viennoiseries and lightly salted butter in portions for the buffet. Monthly invoices with an internal purchase order number.
- **Central kitchens and public catering** (6 customers): Liquid egg products only (HACCP). Purchase order at J-3.

title: Taking an order
body:
- Identify the customer (name, code, or the name of the person calling).
- Suggest « comme d'habitude » based on the latest orders, then confirm quantities.
- Check available stock and today's shortages.
- Read back the order (products, quantities, delivery day) before confirming.
- Check the outstanding balance and account status (blocked?) before validating.

title: Substitutions: never without agreement
body: A missing product is replaced only if the customer agrees. Some customers refuse any substitution (see their profile): call them BEFORE the truck leaves.

title: Blocked customers
body: No deliveries until accounting (Sandrine (comptabilité)) has lifted the block. Take the message, promise nothing.

title: Claims and returns
body:
- Every complaint is logged (customer event) against the order concerned.
- A refusal at delivery is taken back by the driver and deducted from the invoice.
- A credit note above €150 excl. VAT must be approved by management.

title: Selling prices
body:
- Butter and chocolate prices are revised on the 1st of each month (butter quotation, cocoa market prices), and sent to customers on the 25th of the previous month.
- Flours: quarterly price indexed to the miller's wheat; annual price agreements possible for large bakers.
- Frozen, packaging and grocery: annual price list effective 1 February.
- Free-delivery threshold €150 excl. VAT, otherwise €12 delivery charge.
- Discounts: sales reps up to 5%, beyond that Bernard. The switchboard cannot grant any discount.

Resolution order: negotiated customer price > price rule (customer, then group) > list price.

title: Customer groups
body:
- **Boulangeries** (`boulangeries`) : Artisan bakeries: flour by the bag, yeast, laminating butter, packaging.
- **Pâtisseries** (`patisseries`) : Pastry chefs and chocolatiers: couvertures, cream, dried fruit; peaks at Easter and Christmas.
- **Restaurants** (`chr`) : Restaurants and bistros: cream, eggs, butter, some frozen products.
- **Snacking** (`snacking`) : Franchises and sandwich shops: raw viennoiserie by the carton.
- **GMS** (`gms`) : Supermarket bread counters and in-store baking ovens.
- **Traiteurs** (`traiteurs`) : Event caterers, irregular volumes.
- **Hôtellerie** (`hotellerie`) : Hotels: breakfast, monthly invoicing.
- **Collectivités** (`collectivites`) : Central kitchens and public bodies.
- **Marché public** (`marche-public`) : Prices per tender schedule, payment by administrative order.
- **Grands comptes** (`grands-comptes`) : The largest turnover over the last 12 months, monitored by management.
- **À surveiller** (`a-surveiller`) : Late payments, disputes or blocked account: check the outstanding balance before any order.
- **Clients perdus** (`perdus`) : No orders for several months (gone to competitors or closed): to win back.
